newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Macraes to review Reefton mine economics.
newsitem.headline: Macraes to review Reefton mine economics.

text.p: Macraes Mining Company Ltd Chairman Brettney Fogarty said on Thursday the company would reassess the economics of its Reefton gold project on the west coast of New Zealand's South Island after successful drilling in the September quarter.
Fogarty also said he expected gold production at the Macraes project near Dunedin to recover to around 35,000 ounces in the December quarter from 30,762 ounces in the September quarter.

In its quarterly report, Macraes said drilling at Reefton had been successful, with a deep drill hole intersecting the Birthday Reef at 979.6 metres. This was 194 metres below the old workings and returned an assay of 24.6 grams/tonne from an intersection of 0.4 metres.
Fogarty said the intersection was significant.
"It gives us a chance to re-look at the economics of the Reefton gold project over the next six to 12 months," he said in a telephone interview.
He said the company would be developing the Macraes project up until mid-1998 but could use that time to bring Reefton up to the development stage through further exploration and evaluation.
"You're developing one, and then you're bringing the other one up to the development stage," he said.
Development at Reefton was suspended in December 1995 in favour of the Macraes project. Capital costs are estimated at NZ$80 million for Reefton and $120 million for Macraes.
Fogarty said the company was surprised and delighted by a 78 percent rise in reserves at its Macraes gold project near Dunedin to 3.02 million ounces.

"It gives us great encouragement that we're now going to be at the Macraes gold project at that increased rate for a substantial period of time...When you expand, you're always a little bit nervous whether you've overstretched the mark, but we've actually seen very quickly that we haven't."

As previously announced, the company plans to treble ore throughput at Macraes to nine million tonnes a year and boost gold production to 320,000-350,000 ounces a year from 120,000, ranking it among the top five gold producers in Australasia.

Fogarty said production in the next quarter from the Macraes project was expected to recover to 35,000 ounces from 30,762 in the September quarter. The latter was affected by lower grade ore being treated during the period.
He said output was set to remain at 120,000-130,000 ounces in calendar 1997, and the planned expansion would kick in from mid-1998.
